# Delivery routing ruling (e2e synthetic)

Tanya (team owner) ruled on where reaction delivery belongs:

> we route every reaction through one bundle per run per person, not one
> message per skill — a person should get one thing to read, not four

Tina pushed back on the batching window and Tanya held: the bundle closes when
the run closes, and a skill that misses the close waits for the next run rather
than sending on its own. The alternative considered and rejected was per-skill
delivery with client-side collapsing, which moves the ordering problem onto the
reader.

positions.name: ReactionDeliveryBundleBoundary
positions.frame: When many reactions converge on one reader, where does a delivery bundle's boundary fall, and what happens to a reaction that misses the boundary?
positions.why: src-2 states the standing rule (one bundle per run per person) and justifies it by the reader's experience. src-3 sets the boundary (the bundle closes with the run, and a skill that misses the close waits for the next run). src-4 records the rejected alternative, per-skill delivery, and the reason for rejecting it: it moves the ordering problem onto the reader. Read together, the three answer the frame's question about bundling and its boundary. The set holds a tension: src-3 records Tina's pushback on the batching window, which Tanya overruled, and src-2 presents the same rule as settled process. The frame keeps both sides without resolving the disagreement.

placements.title: From per-skill delivery to one bundle per run per person
placements.frame: When many reactions converge on one reader, where does a delivery bundle's boundary fall, and what happens to a reaction that misses that boundary?
placements.why: The three segments carry one continuing subject: how reaction delivery is bundled and where the bundle's boundary falls. src-2 states the standing routing rule (one bundle per run per person). src-3 sets the boundary (the bundle closes with the run, and a skill that misses the close waits for the next run). src-4 records the rejected alternative of per-skill delivery and why it was rejected. The subject is a product-delivery theme that later envelopes about reactions or notifications would keep feeding. None of the existing leaves covers it: AntiSlackPositioning concerns competitive framing, DecisionCaptureAtConsensus concerns capturing decisions, and DecisionsEvaporate concerns decision loss, so no reuse or inspired lineage applies. No strata category is minted, since this is a single leaf with no sibling leaves in a shared region.
